*Sitting down after morning chores, thinking about the year ahead...*

Thirty years I've worked these 10 mu. My wife and I do most of it — the kids send money from the factory but they're not coming back to the field. With 8 mouths on the household register we still keep a little wheat for flour, but mostly I farm for cash now.

I split the land: about **7 mu in wheat-maize** (that's the steady bread-and-butter), and **3.1 mu in chili** on the sandier plot near the road — chili is the money crop if the price holds and the aphids don't eat us alive.

**Wheat** goes in early October, right after the maize comes off. I buy a improved variety from the agri-store in town, nothing fancy. The extension guy at the station says 15 kg N per mu is plenty, but I usually put on a bit more — one 50-jin bag of 复合肥 (compound fertilizer) per mu as base, then topdress about 15 kg of urea at jointing if the field looks pale. I got burned once in a cold spring when I skimped, never again. Three irrigations from the well — after planting, at green-up, and at grain filling. Water isn't free — the electric meter adds up — so I don't pump unless the ground is dry.

**Maize** goes straight in after wheat harvest in mid-June. Tight turnaround, maybe 3-4 days. I hire老王 down the road with his no-till planter-fertilizer combo — costs 30 yuan/mu but saves me from killing myself in the heat. Topdress urea at big trumpet stage. Usually one or two irrigations, depending on summer rains. Summer storms have been less reliable the past few years so I plan for one irrigation for sure.

**Chili** — this is where the work is. Buy transplants from the market in late April. More fertilizer, more spray. My sister-in-law and wife help with picking — pickings run July through October, my back can't do it alone anymore. Good year 400 jin of dried chili per mu, bad year half that. Price is the worry, not yield.

I don't have credit. Whatever I spend has to come out of last year's savings plus the remittances. So I spend where I know it returns — fertilizer on wheat-maize because yield comes straight from it, and pesticide on chili because one bad aphid week wipes out the crop.
